issues.description: The Milkable.messageOnMilk method signature in the solution differs from the problem statement and template. The UML and example usage in the template/Main call messageOnMilk() with no arguments and the problem text specifies messageOnMilk() returning a String (no parameters). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and Seal/Goat implement this signature). This parameter mismatch will cause confusion and compilation errors if students implement the interface as specified in the problem/template or follow the solution as a reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable.messageOnMilk signature across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the volume parameter so the interface declares String messageOnMilk(), and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if a volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement UML and template Main to call messageOnMilk(double) and document the parameter in the specification.

issues.description: The Milkable interface method messageOnMilk is specified and used as a no-argument method in the problem statement and the template Main.java (messageOnMilk(): String), but the solution implements it with a different signature messageOnMilk(double volume). This signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) creates a mapping and compile-time confusion for students: they will expect and be instructed to implement/ call messageOnMilk() without parameters, while the reference solution requires a double parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use messageOnMilk() with no parameters and return the string format "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (matching the problem statement and template Main), or (B) update the problem statement and template usage to specify and call messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the expected output format including the volume. Aligning all three artifacts to the same signature will remove the conceptual and compile-time mismatch.
